_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Read one app or a few...

description: Use this when the user asks about one competitor app, such as "how many installs does this Play app have?" or "when was this app last updated?". Pass app (an App Store id or link, or a Google Play package name or link) and country, or apps with up to 5 of them to compare competitors in one call. Returns the price, rating, rating count, update date, an estimate and a Stale Winner score; for Google Play also exact installs, the rating split and the in-app price range. warnings names each part that is off: App Store IAP tiers, version history and privacy labels, and reviews on both stores. With apps, the answer is reports (one such report per app, in the order asked) and failed (each app that could not be read, with its error code).

app.description: App Store id or link (571800810), or Google Play package name or link (com.calm.android). Do not pass this together with apps.

apps.description: Up to 5 apps to tear down in one call, each in the same form as app, to compare competitors. All share country, store and reviews.

country.description: Two-letter store country, such as us, gb or jp. Default us.

reviews.description: Ask for complaint themes from recent 1 and 2 star reviews. Default true. No allowed source carries reviews, so warnings says so and themes stay empty.

store.description: Force apple or play when the app value is ambiguous, such as an App Store bundle id.

name: app_tracker_lookup

as_of.description: ISO 8601 time the data was published by its source or fetched from it. A cached answer keeps the time of its fetch.

source.description: Who the data comes from, to cite and to check it against.

title: Read one app or a few
